questions.title: Bicycle chain & cogs — radian, angular speed & period

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc whose length is equal to the radius.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
v = rω, so ω = v/r = 17/0.46
= 37 rad s⁻¹

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer:
distance moved = circumference of the small cog = 2πr = 2π × 0.038
= 0.24 m

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.answer:
angle = arc length/radius = 0.24/0.15
= 1.6 rad

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: The rear wheel still rotates at the same angular speed (the bicycle speed is unchanged), but the rear cog is now smaller, so point X on the chain moves through a smaller distance in the same time — the linear speed of the chain decreases. The large cog (fixed to the pedals) has the same radius, so the angular speed of the pedals decreases.

questions.title: Gravitational & magnetic fields of the Earth

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer: A gravitational field line shows the direction of the (gravitational) force that would act on a small test mass placed at that point.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer: At least four radial lines from the Earth’s surface, evenly spaced around it, with arrows pointing towards the centre of the Earth.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: The top pole is labelled S and the bottom pole is labelled N (the geographic north pole is near the Earth’s magnetic south pole).

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: At the poles: at least two field lines on either side of each pole, clustered close together, leaving the surface approximately perpendicular to it and curving away from the pole axis. Above the equator: at least one field line on each side looping from one hemisphere to the other, passing above the surface near the equator approximately parallel to the surface.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer: The gravitational field lines are evenly spaced around the surface and all point perpendicular to the surface (towards the centre), so the field has the same magnitude and direction at every point on the surface — it does not vary around the surface.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer: The magnetic field is strongest at the poles and weakest near the Equator. It is perpendicular to the surface at the poles and parallel to the surface near the Equator, with the angle to the surface increasing from the Equator towards the poles.

questions.title: Specific heat capacity & work done — heated aluminium block

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The (thermal) energy per unit mass required to raise the temperature of the substance by unit temperature (1 K or 1 °C).

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
density = mass/volume, so mass = ρV = 2.700 × 10³ × 3.612 × 10⁻³
= 9.75 kg

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
The mass is constant, so V = V₀ × (ρ₀/ρ) = 3.612 × 10⁻³ × (2.700/2.620)
= 3.722 × 10⁻³ m³

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.answer: The volume of the block increases, so it pushes against the atmosphere and work is done against the atmosphere — the work done on the block is therefore negative.

parts.label: (b)(v)
parts.answer:
From the first law ΔU = q + W, the thermal energy supplied is q = ΔU − W = 4.38 × 10⁶ + 11.1 J (since W is negative).
Specific heat capacity = q/(mΔθ) = 4.38 × 10⁶/(9.75 × 500)
= 898 J kg⁻¹ °C⁻¹

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: Doubling the pressure would double the work done, but the work done (11.1 J) is negligible compared with the change in internal energy (4.38 MJ), so the specific heat capacity would be unchanged.

questions.title: Ideal gases — kinetic theory & mean kinetic energy

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer: T is the thermodynamic temperature (in kelvin).

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer: B is the Boltzmann constant (k).

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: m is the mass of one molecule of the gas, and ⟨c²⟩ is the mean-square speed of the molecules.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
Equating pV from the two equations: NBT/A = ⅓Nm⟨c²⟩. The mean kinetic energy is Ek = ½m⟨c²⟩, so
Ek = 3BT/2A

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: A line with a positive gradient passing through the origin, becoming a smooth curve with a decreasing positive gradient (since cr.m.s. ∝ √T).

questions.title: Simple harmonic motion — displacement, velocity & phase

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Motion in which the acceleration is (directly) proportional to the displacement and is always directed towards a fixed point (in the opposite direction to the displacement).

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
period = 2π/ω = 2π/16
= 0.39 s

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
v₀ = ωx₀, so x₀ = v₀/ω = 0.56/16
= 0.035 m

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.answer: A closed loop (ellipse) surrounding the origin, crossing the x-axis (v = 0) at x = ±3.5 cm and crossing the v-axis (x = 0) at v = ±0.56 m s⁻¹.

questions.title: Electric fields & X-rays — an accelerated electron

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Plate X is negative (−) and plate Y is positive (+) (the electron accelerates towards the positive plate).

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
E = V/x = 58 × 10³/0.041
= 1.4 × 10⁶ N C⁻¹ (equivalent to V m⁻¹)

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer:
The electron gains kinetic energy eV, which is converted to a photon at the minimum wavelength: eV = hc/λ.
λ = hc/eV = (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ × 3.00 × 10⁸)/(1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ × 58 × 10³)
= 2.1 × 10⁻¹¹ m = 21 pm

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer: X-rays.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.answer: The X-rays are passed into the structure and the transmitted waves are detected. Different parts of the structure absorb different fractions of the energy, and the differences in the detected/transmitted intensities are used to form the image.

questions.title: Capacitor discharge — charge, resistance & time constant

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: V<sub>C</sub> = V<sub>R</sub> — the p.d. across the capacitor equals the p.d. across the resistor (they are connected in parallel).

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: Fig. 7.2 and Fig. 7.3 show that charge and current are both directly proportional to the p.d. (so Q ∝ I), and the current is the rate of change of charge. Hence dQ/dt ∝ Q — the charge decreases at a rate proportional to itself, giving an exponential variation.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer: Half-wave rectification.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
P = V²/R, so P₀ = V₀²/R = 8.5²/45
= 1.6 W

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: Over two cycles (t = 0 to 2T): two humps of width 0.5T separated by two sections of zero power of width 0.5T, with peaks at P₀, a smooth sinusoidal shape, and the troughs sitting on the t-axis at P = 0.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer: Within each hump the mean power is ½P₀ (the average of a sin² half-cycle), and only half of each cycle carries any power, so the overall mean power is ½ × ½P₀ = ¼P₀.

questions.title: Photoelectric effect — threshold frequency & work function

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The emission of electrons from a metal surface when electromagnetic radiation is incident on it.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: VS is the stopping voltage — the current falls to zero when the applied p.d. equals the energy per unit charge of the most energetic electrons. The energy of a photon depends on the frequency (E = hf), so the maximum energy of the emitted electrons depends on the photon energy, and therefore VS depends on the frequency.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: Any three of: threshold frequency = 1.5 × 10¹⁵ Hz; threshold wavelength = 2.0 × 10⁻⁷ m; work function = 6.2 eV (9.9 × 10⁻¹⁹ J); Planck constant = 6.6 × 10⁻³⁴ J s; number of photons/electrons per second = 1.7 × 10¹⁶ s⁻¹ (in stage 1); power of the incident radiation = 0.028 W.

questions.title: Radioactive decay — half-life, decay constant & activity

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Decay that is not affected by external/environmental factors — it occurs of its own accord.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
From Fig. 10.1, X halves from 4A to 2A at t = 2T and Y halves from A to ½A at t = 3T, so half-life of X = 2T and half-life of Y = 3T.
Decay constant λ = ln 2/half-life: λX = ln 2/2T, λY = ln 2/3T.
Initial number N₀ = A₀/λ: N₀(X) = 4A/(ln 2/2T) = 8AT/ln 2 and N₀(Y) = A/(ln 2/3T) = 3AT/ln 2.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
Equal activities: 4A e^(−λXt) = A e^(−λYt)
4 = e^(t ln 2(1/2T − 1/3T)) = e^(t ln 2/6T)
ln 4 = t ln 2/6T → 2 ln 2 = t ln 2/6T
t = 12T

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: The count rate is less than the activity because the radiation is emitted in all directions (not just towards the detector), some is absorbed by the air/sample/window of the detector, and some radiation may not register even though it reaches the detector.
